content.text: The Mistake Almost Every Creator Makes First

Many digital creators in Ethiopia and other African countries make the mistake of relying on payment platforms that are not available in their region or have severe restrictions. This can lead to a significant loss of potential sales and revenue. For instance, trying to use Stripe or PayPal in Ethiopia can be a major hurdle, and even if they manage to set up an account, the fees and exchange rates can be exorbitant. Instead, creators should focus on building a sovereign digital commerce stack that is not dependent on these restricted platforms.
Why This Keeps Happening Even to Experienced Sellers

Even experienced sellers can fall into the trap of using payment platforms that are not suitable for their region. This can be due to a lack of awareness about the available alternatives or a misunderstanding of the fees and restrictions associated with popular payment platforms. For example, using USDT on Tron can settle transactions in under 60 seconds for a fee under $0.10, making it a much more attractive option for creators in Ethiopia and other countries with restricted access to traditional payment platforms.
The Real Cost of Getting This Wrong

The real cost of relying on restricted payment platforms can be significant, ranging from lost sales and revenue to damaged reputation and customer trust. When creators are unable to receive payments or deliver products to their customers, it can lead to a loss of credibility and a decline in sales. Furthermore, the fees and exchange rates associated with traditional payment platforms can eat into the creators' profit margins, making it even more challenging to sustain their businesses.
